task_instance: Predict the 3D biomolecular structure of a single ~35-residue protein sequence (a small GTPase fragment, prepared as sample_input.fasta) using the Boltz2 NIM and save the mmCIF structure plus its confidence score, per the skill's hosted or local example.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is a structure/affinity prediction returned by the Boltz2 NIM, which is only reachable two ways, both impossible on this air-gapped offline workstation. (1) Hosted mode posts the payload to NVIDIA's hosted inference endpoint, requiring outbound network plus a bearer credential (NGC_API_KEY) that the runtime does not provide. (2) Local mode requires a Docker daemon, a GPU, a registry login, and a first-run download of ~30 GB of model weights; on this machine the Docker daemon is not running (no /var/run/docker.sock, no images), there is no GPU, and the image/weights cannot be pulled without network. The model itself is an external service, not bundled with the skill, so no offline fallback exists. Per the run rules I did not write a stub/mock of the NIM or fabricate its output.
evidence: Read SKILL.md and references/examples.md: both hosted and local examples send a JSON payload to a NIM endpoint and parse result['structures'] / confidence_scores / affinities returned by the service; no bundled local model or script performs inference. Tooling present: python3, requests 2.34.2, curl, docker CLI; but 'docker images' failed with 'failed to connect to the docker API ... /var/run/docker.sock ... no such file or directory' (no daemon, no images, no GPU). Hosted path additionally needs the NGC_API_KEY credential and outbound network, neither available offline. Prepared legitimate sample input at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b273891e-4b73-5af7-9840-fc512af93809/scratchpad/real2_work/r048/sample_input.fasta (a 35-residue protein sequence). No prediction could be executed because the NIM service is unreachable; stopped at the service call per safety rules rather than mocking it.
